## Introduction

The Palmer Penguins dataset contains measurements for penguins observed
in the Palmer Archipelago of Antarctica. In this analysis, I use Python
to explore how body mass and flipper length vary across penguin species.

The data come from the Palmer Penguins project:
https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/

## Loading the data

I first load the dataset and inspect its structure.

```{python}
#| warning: false

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/allisonhorst/palmerpenguins/main/inst/extdata/penguins.csv"

penguins = pd.read_csv(url)

penguins.head()
```

## Cleaning the data

The variables used in this analysis are species, flipper length, and body
mass. I remove observations that are missing values for these variables.

```{python}
analysis_data = penguins[
    ["species", "flipper_length_mm", "body_mass_g"]
].dropna()

analysis_data.info()
```

## Comparing body mass across species

Next, I calculate the average and median body mass for each penguin species.

```{python}
summary = (
    analysis_data
    .groupby("species")["body_mass_g"]
    .agg(["count", "mean", "median"])
    .round(1)
)

summary
```

The summary shows how typical body mass differs among the three species.

## Relationship between flipper length and body mass

Finally, I visualize the relationship between flipper length and body mass.

```{python}
#| label: fig-penguin-body-mass
#| fig-cap: "Relationship between flipper length and body mass across penguin species"

plt.figure(figsize=(8, 5))

for species, group in analysis_data.groupby("species"):
    plt.scatter(
        group["flipper_length_mm"],
        group["body_mass_g"],
        label=species,
        alpha=0.7
    )

plt.xlabel("Flipper length (mm)")
plt.ylabel("Body mass (g)")
plt.title("Flipper Length and Body Mass by Penguin Species")
plt.legend()
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

The plot shows a positive relationship between flipper length and body mass:
penguins with longer flippers generally tend to have greater body mass.
The species also occupy somewhat different regions of the plot, suggesting
that species is associated with differences in these physical measurements.
